initial_retrieval: Provider-local original BM25 top 20; full arm supplies all operation names
reason: Use a lightweight baseline to isolate automatic expansion; Qdrant remains an optional index. This experiment does not attribute improvements to Qdrant.
adaptive_budget: At most two evidence-expansion/replanning passes after initial discovery and compilation, maximum 12 operations per task and 16 targeted reads per task per expansion. At most one complete-directory fallback per suite.
expansion_signals: Explicit planner operation/schema/policy/external-fact needs, partial requirements, structural/preservation validation issues, used field pointers and response dependency pointers. No private scenario results enter the planner.
quantity_policy: An existing-item price-only Stripe invoice preview requires an explicit typed quantity copy from a completed correctly identified current-item observation. This is an explicitly documented provider boundary rule, not an automatically discovered universal law.
runtime_controls: All arms receive the same preservation schema, policy, planning prompt and guarded runtime. Expansion changes only the evidence and permitted replanning budget.
scoring: Keep the old 52 literal expectations as a frozen score. Separately replay already documented refund-alias and workflow-list fixture corrections. Add strict quantity tests and 41 new frozen scenarios. No silent expectation changes.
inference: Same signed-in default CLI backend; tools disabled. One completed result per stage; operational timeout 240 seconds, one byte-identical retry allowed. Never retry a completed result based on private grades.
fresh_freeze: Freeze new task/scenario definitions before implementation; lock code/prompts/policy before new-fresh model runs. Same author is not blinded.
storage: Canonical source snapshots gzip-compressed with original hashes. Content-addressed gzip blobs deduplicate prompts, payloads and outputs; per-run manifests retain provenance and usage. Generated reports together under documents/generated. Historical artifacts in a verified archive. Never archive secrets or dependency caches.
